This Civil Revision, under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, has been filed against Award dated 06.05.2019 passed by Second Additional District Judge,
Shivpuri (M.P.) in Land Acquisition Case No.400007/2013 by which the reference made by applicant against insufficiency of compensation amount awarded under Land Acquisition Act has been rejected on the ground of delay.

sentences.text: 2. On 28.02.2025, the counsel for applicant had refused to argue on the ground that he did not prepare the case, therefore, by mentioning the conduct of counsel for applicant in detail, this Court heard learned counsel for State.

3. The first question for consideration is as to whether a Civil Revision is maintainable against award passed by the Reference Court under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short "the Act") or not?
4.
In the present case, the Reference was dismissed on the ground of delay.

5. Earlier, the Supreme Court in the case of Ratan Singh Vs. Vijaysingh reported in (2001) 1 SCC 469 had held that dismissal of an application for condonation of delay and consequent dismissal of appeal as barred by time, would not be a decree.

entities.text: Ratan Singh Vs. Vijaysingh reported in (2001) 1 SCC 469
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, later on, in the case of Shyam Sundar Sarma vs Pannalal Jaiswal And Others NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:5113 reported in (2005)1 SCC 436, it was held that the law laid down in the case of Ratan Singh (Supra), is not the correct law.

entities.text: Shyam Sundar Sarma vs Pannalal Jaiswal And Others NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:5113 reported in (2005)1 SCC 436
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, it is clear that even if a case is dismissed as barred by time, still it would be a decree, which is liable to be assailed by filing a regular appeal.

In the Act,
the only remedy available to challenge the Award is to file first appeal under section 54 of the Act.

Since reference was dismissed on the ground of delay, therefore,
applicant should have preferred first appeal under section 54 of the Act.

6. Furthermore, in the light of judgment passed by Full Bench of this Court in State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Seth Gowardhandas Maheshwari reported in 1993 MPLJ 536, it is clear that applicant has to pay Ad Valorem court fee computed according to the difference between the amount awarded and amount claimed by applicant as per the mandate of S.8 of the Court Fees Act, on which Court fee, as prescribed under Article 1A of Schedule 1 of the Court Fees Act has to be paid.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, the Court fee has not been computed according to the difference between the amount awarded and amount claimed by applicant.

Under these circumstances, even this Civil Surendra Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34601051/
2 Revision cannot be permitted to be converted into First Appeal.

sentences.text: 7. The application under S.18 of the Act should have been made within a period of six weeks from the date of Award passed by the Collector in case if applicant was present and in other cases, within a period of 6 weeks of receipt of notice from Collector under section 12, sub-section (2) or within six months from the date of Collector's Award, whichever period shall first expire.

In the present case, Reference Court has given a specific finding that applicant was present before the Land Acquisition Officer on 8/8/2012 and applicant has also admitted her signatures in the order-sheet dated 8/8/2012.
By order dated 8/8/2012, case was fixed for passing of Award on 24/8/2012.
Thus, it is clear that applicant was present at the time of passing of Award and, therefore, Reference Court did not commit any mistake by holding that the Reference was barred by time.
8. Accordingly, this Court is of considered opinion that no case is made out warranting interference.
9. Revision fails and is, hereby, dismissed, on the ground of maintainability as well as on merits.

Accordingly, this revision also stands dismissed on the term and conditions as mentioned in the order passed in the case of Smt. Shimlesh (Supra).
